Root cause and fix are in probe-usermsg-fix-results.json — the fixed user message presupposed a challengeable claim on every call; the NONE clause in the system prompt alone couldn't reliably override that. Left in place for history; do not treat the summary/verdict below as current.
prompt_version: baseline-v1 + none-escape-valve (read live from lib/probe.ts at run time)
reviewer_notes: PART 1 (revert): production PROBE_SYSTEM was first restored byte-for-byte to the frozen baseline (PROBE_SYSTEM_VERBATIM in probe-baseline.ts) — verified byte-identical (650 chars). PART 2 then appended ONLY the NONE escape valve; everything before that clause remains byte-identical to the baseline.

A first NONE clause (soft wording) produced 0/5 declines — the model still fabricated a question for every clean paragraph, because the fixed user message ('what question would most challenge it?') presupposes a question exists. The clause was strengthened (explicit override of that framing + three domain-neutral category examples of NONE-worthy text) WITHOUT touching the user message or the eligibility gate. That produced the numbers below.
The eval reads the live production PROBE_SYSTEM directly from src/lib/probe.ts (not a frozen copy) and aborts if the NONE clause is absent — so these numbers reflect exactly what is deployed.

Recall answers differ from the original baseline run wording (e.g. R1) due to the documented Groq/Llama temperature-0 non-determinism (see Trial 5 infrastructure_note); the metric that matters is that all five still returned real questions (0 NONE), i.e. no real flag was suppressed.
